facts.t: The CAG can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge
facts.d: Article 148 applies the impeachment standard — proved misbehaviour or incapacity, with a special majority in both Houses. The salary is charged on the Consolidated Fund, so Parliament cannot vote it down either.

facts.t: Two audit reports cancelled hundreds of licences
facts.d: The 2G report led the Supreme Court to cancel 122 telecom licences; the Coalgate report underpinned the cancellation of 214 coal block allocations. No other Indian institution has produced documents with that direct legal consequence.

facts.t: America's auditor keeps a High-Risk List
facts.d: The GAO publishes a running register of vulnerable federal programmes and tracks each until resolved. India's CAG has no equivalent follow-up mechanism — its recommendations carry no binding force at all.

bank.q: The CAG's duties and powers are prescribed by:
bank.e: Article 149 empowers Parliament, which enacted the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971.

bank.q: With reference to the CAG's constitutional position, consider the following:
s: The salary is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
Removal follows the same procedure as for a Supreme Court judge.
Reports on State accounts are submitted to the President.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. State reports go to the Governor and are laid before the State Legislature.

bank.q: Match List I (article) with List II (function):
pairs: 1. Accounting formats prescribed on the CAG's advice
2. Appointment and removal of the CAG
3. Certification of net proceeds of taxes
bank.e: Article 148 on appointment, 150 on accounting formats, 151 on reports, and 279 on certifying net proceeds for Centre-State distribution.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a type of audit conducted by the CAG?
o: Pre-audit clearance of major government contracts
bank.e: India lacks strong ex-ante financial control — introducing real-time or concurrent audit for large contracts is a reform proposal, not existing practice.

bank.as: The CAG is described as the friend, philosopher and guide to the Public Accounts Committee.
bank.rs: Its reports supply the factual basis on which the PAC examines government expenditure.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the audit-to-PAC pipeline is the core accountability mechanism.

bank.q: Consider the following criticisms of the CAG:
s: Audits are post-facto, limiting real-time correction.
Recommendations carry no binding enforcement power.
Public-private partnerships and autonomous societies fall fully within its effective reach.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Coverage gaps over PPPs, autonomous societies and NGOs receiving public funds are a recognised problem.

bank.q: Which case upheld the CAG's authority to audit private telecom providers?
o: Association of Unified Telecom Service Providers v. UoI
bank.e: The 2014 judgment, confined to the extent of their revenue-sharing arrangements with the government.

bank.q: Match List I (country) with List II (audit practice):
pairs: 1. Reports directly to the legislature with a High-Risk List
2. Real-time and concurrent audit inputs into budget-making
3. Value-for-money audits with a mandatory government response deadline
4. Sunset review requiring departments to report corrective action
bank.e: The National Audit Office's response deadlines, the GAO's High-Risk List, the Bundesrechnungshof's concurrent inputs, and Canada's sunset reviews.

bank.q: All of the following are proposed reforms EXCEPT:
o: A collegium for appointment including the Chief Justice and Leader of the Opposition
Legally binding timelines for Action Taken Reports
Restricting audit jurisdiction to core government departments
Building forensic accounting and IT audit capacity
bank.e: The proposal runs the other way — expanding jurisdiction to PPPs, large NGOs and autonomous bodies receiving substantial public funds.

bank.q: With reference to landmark audits, consider the following:
s: The 2G audit flagged first-come-first-served allocation without auction.
The Coalgate audit led to the cancellation of over 200 allocations.
The Commonwealth Games audit found cost overruns and procurement irregularities.
bank.e: All three are correct — collectively the strongest demonstration of audit translating into legal consequence.

bank.q: Under which provision does the CAG audit government companies?
bank.e: Section 143 of the Companies Act, 2013 governs the audit of government companies, alongside statutory corporations under their own enactments.
